feed.title: Btc-verified October Update: Connecting Map to Territory

entry.title: Btc-verified October Update: Connecting Map to Territory
entry.summary:
A standalone differential fuzzing harness has been developed for Bitcoin Core and btc-verified, concentrating on the kernel interface. This tool targets nine critical kernel functions supported by a Lean implementation, which encompass transaction creation, copying, serialization, validation, and the management of associated validation-state objects. The objective is to ensure both Bitcoin Core and btc-verified handle identical transaction bytes consistently, with the harness facilitating direct behavioral comparisons.
The harness is constructed atop [libFuzzer](https://llvm.org/docs/LibFuzzer.html), a widely-used fuzzing engine, allowing for efficient input generation and automated comparison of outputs. Full documentation for this harness and its usage can be found in the corresponding [README file](https://github.com/ProofOfKeags/btc-verified/blob/5cd2d824784dc2fac33aec641a0e10fcf869d0b2/Fuzz/README.md). Details regarding the public C interface for the nine kernel functions are also available [here](https://github.com/ProofOfKeags/btc-verified/blob/5cd2d824784dc2fac33aec641a0e10fcf869d0b2/Kernel/README.mdpublic-c-interface).
Integration of this approach into bitcoinfuzz was straightforward due to the existing support for libbitcoinkernel. The process primarily involved adding btc-verified as a new module and implementing a new fuzzing target, modeled after existing internal targets. A pull request reflecting these changes can be reviewed at [bitcoinfuzz PR #681](https://github.com/bitcoinfuzz/bitcoinfuzz/pull/681), demonstrating successful adaptation and extension of the fuzzing infrastructure.
